cases.sentence: Вы ___ жужжите, всё жужжите — как не надоест!
cases.explain: «целый день» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: HELENA. I wonder you are not bored, droning on in the same key from morning till night. [Despairingly] I am dying of this tedium. What shall I do?

cases.sentence: Это только в ___ учат и лечат мужиков, а как я, ни с того ни с сего, возьму вдруг и пойду их лечить или учить?
cases.explain: «идейных романах» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: HELENA. I don't know anything about such things, and besides, they don't interest me. It is only in novels that women go out and teach and heal the peasants; how can I suddenly begin to do it?

cases.sentence: Дайте себе волю хоть раз в жизни, влюбитесь поскорее в какого-нибудь водяного по ___ — и бултых с головой в омут, чтобы герр профессор и все мы только руками развели!
cases.explain: «самые уши» — after the preposition «по», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: VOITSKI. Why should you languish here? Come, my dearest, my beauty, be sensible! The blood of a Nixey runs in your veins. Oh, won't you let yourself be one? Give your nature the reins for once in your life; fall head over ears in love with some other water sprite and plunge down head first into a deep pool, so that the Herr Professor and all of us may have our hands free again.

cases.sentence: ___ — прелестные, грустные розы…

cases.translation: VOITSKI. As a peace offering I am going to fetch some flowers which I picked for you this morning: some autumn roses, beautiful, sorrowful roses. [He goes out.]

cases.explain: «грустные розы» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: Откладывать в ___ не будем, допросим его теперь же.
cases.explain: «долгий ящик» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: SONIA nods. HELENA. It will be easier not to see him any more. We won't put off the examination an instant. He said he had a sketch to show me. Go and tell him at once that I want to see him.

cases.sentence: Она некрасива, но для ___, в его годы, это была бы прекрасная жена.
cases.explain: «деревенского доктора» — after the preposition «для», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: HELENA. [Alone] There is no greater sorrow than to know another's secret when you cannot help them. [In deep thought] He is obviously not in love with her, but why shouldn't he marry her? She is not pretty, but she is so clever and pure and good, she would make a splendid wife for a country doctor of his years. [A pause] I can understand how the poor child feels. She lives here in this desperate loneliness with no one around her except these colourless shadows that go mooning about talking nonsense and knowing nothing except that they eat, drink, and sleep. Among them appears from time to time this Dr. Astroff, so different, so handsome, so interesting, so charming. It is like seeing the moon rise on a dark night. Oh, to surrender oneself to his embrace! To lose oneself in his arms! I am a little in love with him myself! Yes, I am lonely without him, and when I think of him I smile. That Uncle Vanya says I have the blood of a Nixey in my veins: "Give rein to your nature for once in your life!" Perhaps it is right that I should. Oh, to be free as a bird, to fly away from all your sleepy faces and your talk and forget that you have existed at all! But I am a coward, I am afraid; my conscience torments me. He comes here every day now. I can guess why, and feel guilty already; I should like to fall on my knees at Sonia's feet and beg her forgiveness, and weep.

cases.sentence: (Растягивает на ___ картограмму и укрепляет ее кнопками.) Вы где родились?
cases.explain: «ломберном столе» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: He lays the portfolio on the table, takes out the sketch and fastens it to the table with thumb-tacks. ASTROFF. Where were you born?

cases.sentence: Здесь в доме есть мой ___…
cases.explain: «собственный стол» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: ASTROFF. I have my own desk there in Ivan's room. When I am absolutely too exhausted to go on I drop everything and rush over here to forget myself in this work for an hour or two. Ivan and Miss Sonia sit rattling at their counting-boards, the cricket chirps, and I sit beside them and paint, feeling warm and peaceful. But I don't permit myself this luxury very often, only once a month. [Pointing to the picture] Look there! That is a map of our country as it was fifty years ago. The green tints, both dark and light, represent forests. Half the map, as you see, is covered with it. Where the green is striped with red the forests were inhabited by elk and wild goats. Here on this lake, lived great flocks of swans and geese and ducks; as the old men say, there was a power of birds of every kind. Now they have vanished like a cloud. Beside the hamlets and villages, you see, I have dotted down here and there the various settlements, farms, hermit's caves, and water-mills. This country carried a great many cattle and horses, as you can see by the quantity of blue paint. For instance, see how thickly it lies in this part; there were great herds of them here, an average of three horses to every house. [A pause] Now, look lower down. This is the country as it was twenty-five years ago. Only a third of the map is green now with forests. There are no goats left and no elk. The blue paint is lighter, and so on, and so on. Now we come to the third part; our country as it appears to-day. We still see spots of green, but not much. The elk, the swans, the black-cock have disappeared. It is, on the whole, the picture of a regular and slow decline which it will evidently only take about ten or fifteen more years to complete. You may perhaps object that it is the march of progress, that the old order must give place to the new, and you might be right if roads had been run through these ruined woods, or if factories and schools had taken their place. The people then would have become better educated and healthier and richer, but as it is, we have nothing of the sort. We have the same swamps and mosquitoes; the same disease and want; the typhoid, the diphtheria, the burning villages. We are confronted by the degradation of our country, brought on by the fierce struggle for existence of the human race. It is the consequence of the ignorance and unconsciousness of starving, shivering, sick humanity that, to save its children, instinctively snatches at everything that can warm it and still its hunger. So it destroys everything it can lay its hands on, without a thought for the morrow. And almost everything has gone, and nothing has been created to take its place. [Coldly] But I see by your face that I am not interesting you.

cases.sentence: Мне нужно сделать вам ___, и я смущена, не знаю, как начать.
cases.explain: «маленький допрос» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: HELENA. Frankly, my thoughts were elsewhere. Forgive me! I want to submit you to a little examination, but I am embarrassed and don't know how to begin.

cases.sentence: Фу, какой ___!
cases.explain: «неприятный разговор» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: HELENA. Bah! What an unpleasant conversation! I am as out of breath as if I had been running three miles uphill. Thank heaven, that is over! Now let us forget everything as if nothing had been said. You are sensible. You understand. [A pause] I am actually blushing.

cases.sentence: Вы ___, поймете…
cases.explain: «умный человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: HELENA. Bah! What an unpleasant conversation! I am as out of breath as if I had been running three miles uphill. Thank heaven, that is over! Now let us forget everything as if nothing had been said. You are sensible. You understand. [A pause] I am actually blushing.

cases.sentence: Хищница милая, не смотрите на меня так, я ___…
cases.explain: «старый воробей» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: ASTROFF. [Laughing] You are a wily one! I admit that Sonia is suffering, but what does this examination of yours mean? [He prevents her from retorting, and goes on quickly] Please don't put on such a look of surprise; you know perfectly well why I come here every day. Yes, you know perfectly why and for whose sake I come! Oh, my sweet tigress! don't look at me in that way; I am an old bird!

cases.sentence: Вот я уже ___ ничего не делаю, бросил все, жадно ищу вас — и это вам ужасно нравится, ужасно…
cases.explain: «целый месяц» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: ASTROFF. Beautiful, sleek tigress, you must have your victims! For a whole month I have done nothing but seek you eagerly. I have thrown over everything for you, and you love to see it. Now then, I am sure you knew all this without putting me through your examination. [Crossing his arms and bowing his head] I surrender. Here you have me--now, eat me.

cases.sentence: (В ___ отходит к окну.) Это ужасно.
cases.explain: «сильном смущении» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: HELENA. [Sees VOITSKI] Let me go! [Goes to the window deeply embarrassed] This is appalling!

cases.sentence: Двадцать шесть ___, разбредутся все, и никого никогда не найдешь.
cases.explain: «громадных комнат» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: SEREBRAKOFF. Where are the others? I hate this house. It is a regular labyrinth. Every one is always scattered through the twenty-six enormous rooms; one never can find a soul. [Rings] Ask my wife and Madame Voitskaya to come here!

cases.sentence: Деньги обратить в ___ и на излишек, какой останется, купить дачу в Финляндии.
cases.explain: «процентные бумаги» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: SEREBRAKOFF. I said we would invest the money in bonds and buy a cottage in Finland with the surplus.

cases.sentence: Ты продашь имение, превосходно, ___…
cases.explain: «богатая идея» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: VOITSKI. Aha! That was it! So you are going to sell the place? Splendid. The idea is a rich one. And what do you propose to do with my old mother and me and with Sonia here?

cases.sentence: Очевидно, до сих пор у меня не было ни капли ___.
cases.explain: «здравого смысла» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: VOITSKI. Wait! It is clear that until this moment I have never had a grain of sense in my head. I have always been stupid enough to think that the estate belonged to Sonia. My father bought it as a wedding present for my sister, and I foolishly imagined that as our laws were made for Russians and not Turks, my sister's estate would come down to her child.

cases.sentence: Мой ___ купил это имение в приданое для моей сестры.
cases.explain: «покойный отец» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: Я, ваше превосходительство, питаю к науке не только благоговение, но и ___.
cases.explain: «родственные чувства» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: TELEGIN. [With embarrassment] I not only nourish feelings of respect toward learning, your Excellency, but I am also drawn to it by family ties. My brother Gregory's wife's brother, whom you may know; his name is Constantine Lakedemonoff, and he used to be a magistrate--

cases.sentence: Это имение было куплено по ___ за девяносто пять тысяч.
cases.explain: «тогдашнему времени» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: VOITSKI. The price was ninety-five thousand roubles. My father paid seventy and left a debt of twenty-five. Now listen! This place could never have been bought had I not renounced my inheritance in favour of my sister, whom I deeply loved--and what is more, I worked for ten years like an ox, and paid off the debt.

cases.sentence: Имение чисто от долгов и не расстроено только благодаря моим ___.
cases.explain: «личным усилиям» — after the preposition «благодаря», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: VOITSKI. Thanks entirely to my own personal efforts, the place is entirely clear of debts, and now, when I have grown old, you want to throw me out, neck and crop!

cases.sentence: Двадцать пять лет я управлял этим имением, работал, высылал тебе деньги, как самый ___, и за все время ты ни разу не поблагодарил меня.
cases.explain: «добросовестный приказчик» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: VOITSKI. For twenty-five years I have managed this place, and have sent you the returns from it like the most honest of servants, and you have never given me one single word of thanks for my work, not one--neither in my youth nor now. You allowed me a meagre salary of five hundred roubles a year, a beggar's pittance, and have never even thought of adding a rouble to it.

cases.sentence: Зачем портить ___?
cases.explain: «хорошие отношения» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: TELEGIN. [Agitated] Vanya, old man, don't talk in that way. Why spoil such pleasant relations? [He embraces him] Do stop!

cases.sentence: (В ___ уходит.)
cases.explain: «сильном волнении» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: TELEGIN. I can't stand it; I can't stand it. I am going. [He goes out in great excitement.]
